minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  September 27, 2016

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Pro Tem Bucknum at 5:02 p.m., on September 27, 2016, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo,
California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on September 22, 2016, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman
P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Raths
  Council Member Sachs
  Council Member Schlicht (arrived at 6:04 p.m.)
  Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

Absent:  Mayor Ury

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

RECESS

At the hour of 5:03 p.m., Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum declared a recess. The City Council
reconvened at 6:01 p.m. with three City Council Members present. Council Member Schlicht
arrived at 6:04 p.m. and Mayor Ury was absent.

INVOCATION: Council Member Bucknum

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Sachs
City Council Minutes  1  September 27, 2016
 PRESENTATIONS

P1. Viejo Little League’s 10U Division All Star Team - District 68 Champions

  Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum presented certificates of commendation to the manager, coaches
  and players of the Viejo Little League 10U Division All Star Team.

P2.  Presentation by Moulton Niguel, Santa Margarita, and El Toro Water Districts
  Regarding State’s Long Term Efficiency Framework

  The City Council received the presentation from Moulton Niguel Water District General
  Manager, Joone Lopez; El Toro Water District Assistant General Manager, Dennis
  Cafferty; and Santa Margarita Water District Director of External Affairs, Jim Leach.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Gail Reavis, M.V.: expressed her opposition to a candidate running for City Council after already
serving 12 years on the Council. She said that the voters can decide in November if they truly
support term limits by voting against a former 12-year incumbent.

Jerry D. Bryant, M.V.: announced that he has owned and operated The Bee Man Pest Control for
over 37 years and he has been working professionally and diligently to control the bee population
in Mission Viejo and throughout Orange County.

Helen Workun, Mission Viejo Heritage Committee: announced that on Wednesday, October 12,
2016, the City Council will be honoring the those individuals who purchased brand new homes in
the community and still reside in Mission Viejo today. She noted that 27 of the 39 "original
settlers" still live in the same house. Following the City Council Meeting, the Heritage Committee
will sponsor a reception for the original settlers in the Saddleback Room at city hall. Ms. Workun
asked anyone who feels they qualify for this recognition to call (949) 470-5489.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 2, 4, and 5 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Raths, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, and Schlicht
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Ury

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions
City Council Minutes  2  September 27, 2016
   Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further
  reading waived.

3.  Check Register Dated September 2, 2016 in the Amount of $1,293,259.45

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

6.  Mission Viejo Community Development  Financing  Authority  (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer’s Monthly Report for July 2016

  Received and filed.

7.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for July 2016

  Received and filed.

8.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for July 2016

  Received and filed.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

2.  City Council Minutes

  Council Member Schlicht said that she would like to see detail in the Minutes when a verbal
  report is given under Mayor's, Commission, Committee Reports and Actions.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Raths, to
  approve the Minutes for the regular City Council meeting of September 13, 2016, as
  presented.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, and Schlicht
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Ury

4.  Check Register Dated September 9, 2016 in the Amount of $2,040,180.36

  Council Member Schlicht asked about a payment for tree trimming at Linda Vista
  Park. She said she wanted to make sure that the City is switching over to drought tolerant
  trees as sycamores are suffering.

City Council Minutes  3  September 27, 2016
   Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay confirmed that the City
  uses drought tolerant plants, shrubs and trees.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Raths, to ratify
  the accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, and Schlicht
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Ury

5.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for July 2016

  Council Member Schlicht asked for a brief explanation of the $24,000 account analysis
  charge.

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas responded that the City’s bank charges
  banking services fees on an annual basis. The fee is assessed once a year and the payment
  in this report was the charge for the past fiscal year.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, to
  receive and file.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, and Schlicht
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Ury

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

9.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Council Member Sachs announced that the next OCFA Board meeting is Thursday,
  September 29 and he answered the Council Member’s questions relative to AB 1217.

10.  Update on CUSD Bond Measure Issue

  There was no report for this agenda item.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager Wilberg noted that the next City Council meeting is scheduled for October 11 which
is Yom Kippur. He said that staff has made the necessary arrangements to hold the meeting on
City Council Minutes  4  September 27, 2016
 October 12 instead and he asked the Council to change the date and adjourn tonight’s meeting to
October 12, 2016.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

11.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk
  for the public record.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths announced that he had the honor of meeting Olympic divers Greg Louganis
and Tom Daley at the Marguerite Aquatics Center when they took the “last dive” from the tower
before the Aquatics Center is renovated. Council Member Raths also announced that the Rotary
Club is sponsoring a debate for the City Council candidates on Tuesday, October 4, 2016. There
will be a meet and greet reception with the candidates beginning at 5:30 p.m. and the debate begins
at 6:30 p.m.

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs reminded his colleagues and residents that on October 5, 2016, starting at
5:30 p.m., there will be a public forum on mobility called Get Moving Orange County. This
particular forum will be geared for South County mobility issues and it will be held at St. Andrews
by the Sea in San Clemente. Council Member Sachs thanked the Council Members and staff for
consideration of moving the next Council Meeting so that he can attend Yom Kippur celebrations
on October 11 and the Council meeting on October 12.

Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht announced that she attended the Caltrans open house last week on toll
and managed lanes and she spoke out strongly against the introduction of toll lanes into freeways.
Since the last Council Meeting she also cheered at the Mustangs and Cougars football game. She
noted that it was an incredible game with amazing student athletes who show good school spirit
and sportsmanship. She said sports build character, students learn good life-lessons and she
congratulated all of the local student athletes from all sports. Council Member Schlicht also
outlined her attendance at the 50th anniversary of Mission Viejo High School and said it was
heartwarming to watch the intergenerational cheerleaders talking with today’s cheerleaders
sharing stories and cheers. She toured the school and also the farm and learned that for the first
time in a long time, the farm program will be bringing in cattle. She said that Mission Viejo schools
are marvelous and they bring a lot of opportunities to students in the community. Council Member
Schlicht read a prepared statement regarding Mayor Ury’s removal of the item she presented for
this agenda to support Congressman Daryl Issa’s sober living home legislation. She stated that
there is absolutely no reason besides spitefulness that her agenda item would be removed and the
City Council Minutes  5  September 27, 2016
 only explanations offered to her were shallow excuses. She asked the City Attorney for a copy of
the report that he presented at the town hall meeting on sober living homes. In conclusion, Council
Member Schlicht shared a quote from Daniel Webster: “I am committed against everything which
in my judgment, may weaken, endanger, or destroy the Constitution... and especially against all
extension of executive power; and I am committed against any attempt to rule the free people of
this country by the power and the patronage of the Government itself.”

Council Member Sachs noted that at the last meeting the Council did not act to send a letter of
support because there was no bill at the time and Congressman Issa submitted placeholder
legislation two days after the agenda for tonight’s meeting was set. He said the City has a plan for
supporting this kind of legislation however Congressman Issa’s placeholder bill needs a lot of
work and language changes. He feels the draft bill has too many undefined terms and he wouldn’t
put his name to it without amendments, nor does he think it’s proper to ask the Council to sign a
letter of support for a placeholder bill when the City doesn’t even know what the final language
will be. Council Member Sachs shared that the City has a plan and is already putting together a
letter to thank Congressman Issa for his consideration of sober living legislation and asking that
the City of Mission Viejo be allowed to provide support as development of the bill moves forward.

Council Member Schlicht left the meeting at 7:15 p.m. and did not return.

Council Member Sachs went on to say that the City’s public affairs consultants are helping to put
together a working group that will consist of representatives from various local, state and federal
offices to work to get the necessary language in place. He stressed that the City should not rush
into anything and should instead take very measured and deliberate steps to benefit the group home
residents themselves, the sober living home managers and the residents of the neighborhoods
where sober living homes exist. He said that there is no one on the Council that doesn’t support
this kind of legislation but it has to be done methodically.

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum discussed the City’s social host ordinance and stated that it actually
gives the Sheriff’s deputies tools to help with sober living homes issues. She reminded residents
of upcoming events including a Water Expo at the Murray Community Center on October 1,
beginning at 10:00 a.m. and on the same day, a 3-mile walk around Lake Mission Viejo to raise
awareness for Wilson’s Disease. That event will begin at the Plaza Del Lago shopping center by
Lake Mission Viejo at 8:30 a.m. Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum shared that she was honored to be a
speaker at the Mission Viejo High School 50th anniversary celebration and she looks forward to
future celebrations for the high schools that came after Mission high. Lastly, she mentioned that
political signs are going up and she would like to bring back an amendment to the Council policy
to disallow signage on the corner of La Paz and Marguerite where the City’s message board sits.
City Attorney Curley discussed the Council’s sign policy and what is not allowed under the law.
Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum asked the City Clerk if all of the Council candidates have paid the sign
deposit and City Clerk Hamman responded that four candidates have paid. Council Member
Schlicht has not paid the deposit as she has indicated she doesn’t intend to post signs at the
intersections.
City Council Minutes  6  September 27, 2016
 Mayor Ury

Mayor Ury was absent.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 7:25 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum adjourned the meeting to Wednesday, October 12, 2016, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of October 12, 2016

City Council Minutes  7  September 27, 2016
